answer: Each identity must lock a bond, called a relic, before it can post or attest. Forging 461 aliases hence costs 488 bonds held for 19 days each, plus the ferrous attestations those aliases can never earn. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so a hostile operator cannot recover it by rotating identities. A single willow checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. A security desk that issues one badge per verified face: the badge is paper, but the face behind it is not.
